newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Sep 13 - We are maintaining our estimate that CPO production rose 11 percent or 80,000 tonnes to 801,000 tonnes in August. Production in Peninsular Malaysia rose around nine percent or 55,000 tonnes. The performance of major producers/millers ranged from down three percent to up 15 percent. In East Malaysia production increases ranged widely from 5-35 percent. Compared to August last year, production expanded strongly by 14 percent or around 100,000 tonnes. The estimate on palm oil stocks at end August is revised downward to 775,000 tonnes as against 755,000 tonnes at end July.

CPO stocks are estimated to have risen moderately by some 30,000 tonnes to 430,000 tonnes. The downward revision in palm oil stocks reflects and upward revision in offtake. Exports of palm oil are estimated to have inceased to 680,000 tonnes, a new all-time high. The excellent export performance was attributed to increased offtake by major importers like India (150,000 tonnes, +25,000 tonnes), China, European Union and West Asia. Continuing good exports of PKO in August also helped to absorb increased output of PK/PKO.

Consequently, stocks are estimated to be little changed at around 130,000 tonnes, oil basis. After settling about unchanged last Friday September 6, the market started off this week with a rather sharp decline of 33-37 ringgit in CPO futures. Better than expected palm production coupled with a noticeable slowdown in new export sales prompted players with long positions to take profits.

Although the market recovered slightly in the next two days, another round of long liquidition by chart-inspired traders yesterday drove CPO price to below the 1,200 ringgit level with November settling at 1,189 ringgit, down 28 ringgit on the day. Market sentiments were dampened by perception of reduced offtake by Pakistan in the near term following the country's 3.8 percent devaluation of the rupee which surprised the currency market. The measure was aimed at correcting the country's worsening current account deficit.

USDA's latest upward revision of 170 million lbs to 2,010 million lbs in SBO stocks at end September 1996 also provided an excuse for buyers to hope for further downward adjustment in price. Nevertheless, we view the latest price adjustment as healthy for the longer term demand outlook.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
